newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower after samurais fail to show.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower after samurais fail to show.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended lower on Tuesday after rumoured samurai issues failed to show.
Kiwi ended at US$0.7097/04 and 66.85 on the Trade Weighted Index from 0.7123/30, 67.11 at the open.
Stop losses were triggered at 0.7090, taking the Kiwi to a low of 0.7086.
Dealers said Kiwi had been bought on Monday in anticipation of more dual currency issues.

"People have been talking about more samurais but I think that it's been more rumour than anything backed up. Nothing's materialised so the market has been caught a bit long over the last few days," said one dealer.
Short term, he expected 0.7115-20 to be the top for the Kiwi with support around 0.7070-80.
If fresh samurai issuance failed to materialise, the currency may well hit 0.7050-60, he said.

One other dealer said comments on a wire service from Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen saying that he expected an easing of monetary policy sooner rather than later was responsible for a 15-basis-point selloff.
He said the comment caught the local and offshore players a little long.
"But we continue to see demand so I don't think anthing has changed. It's just another of the dips that we see from time to time," he said. He expected an overnight range of 0.7080-30.
